speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your symptoms in detail, specifically regarding the onset, duration, and character of your vomiting and chest pain. To help me prioritize, have you experienced any shortness of breath, sweating, or pain radiating to your arm or jaw?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture). The history of forceful vomiting (retching) followed immediately by severe chest pain and coughing is the classic presentation for this life-threatening esophageal tear. I am requesting a CT of the chest with oral contrast and a Chest_X-Ray to confirm the diagnosis and look for pleural effusion or pneumothorax.
